environmentVariables.description: BAM base URL (e.g., https://bam.bluecat.com).
environmentVariables.name: BAM_BASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: BAM service-account username. Required unless the SSO pair (BAM_SSO_USERNAME + BAM_SSO_PASSWORD) is used instead — the server needs exactly one of the two pairs.
environmentVariables.name: BAM_USERNAME

environmentVariables.description: BAM service-account password. Required alongside BAM_USERNAME, unless the SSO pair is used instead.
environmentVariables.name: BAM_PASSWORD

environmentVariables.description: BAM SSO username. Alternative to BAM_USERNAME + BAM_PASSWORD; the server needs exactly one of the two pairs.
environmentVariables.name: BAM_SSO_USERNAME

environmentVariables.description: BAM SSO password. Required alongside BAM_SSO_USERNAME when using the SSO pair.
environmentVariables.name: BAM_SSO_PASSWORD

environmentVariables.description: Client authentication mode for the /mcp endpoint. One of: none | static-key | signed-key | resource-server. Required at runtime — the server refuses to start without it (no default).
environmentVariables.name: MCP_AUTH_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Static bearer token clients present as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Required only when MCP_AUTH_MODE=static-key.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: HMAC key (at least 32 bytes) sealing the approval-gated write tools' requestState on MCP 2026-07-28 connections (#1031). Optional: unset uses a random per-process key, which is fine for a single replica; set the same value on every replica of a multi-replica deployment.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_REQUEST_STATE_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Second requestState HMAC key, accepted for opening a sealed plan but never for sealing one: two-key rotation of MCP_REQUEST_STATE_KEY (#1032). Optional, and only valid together with MCP_REQUEST_STATE_KEY. When rolling the key across replicas set this to the old key, and remove it two minutes after the last replica restarted.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_REQUEST_STATE_KEY_PREVIOUS

environmentVariables.description: Ed25519 public key (base64url) that MCP_AUTH_MODE=signed-key verifies license tokens against. DEFAULTS TO A SHARED DEMO KEY, which authenticates a token holder rather than a customer — every BlueCat-issued token for this server verifies against it. For anything beyond a trial, generate a per-deployment key pair (license-keygen --gen-key) and set this to its public half.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_ED25519_PUBLIC_KEY

environmentVariables.description: When set, a license token must carry exactly this audience or it is rejected — a declarative scope check on top of the key, so a token minted for another deployment fails even if it verifies. Unset means the aud claim is not checked. Only meaningful with MCP_AUTH_MODE=signed-key.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_SIGNED_KEY_AUDIENCE

environmentVariables.description: Token issuer URL, matched against the iss claim of incoming JWTs. Required when MCP_AUTH_MODE=resource-server — the server refuses to start in that mode without it.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER

environmentVariables.description: JWKS endpoint whose public keys verify the signature on every incoming Bearer JWT. Required when MCP_AUTH_MODE=resource-server — the server refuses to start in that mode without it.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_OAUTH_JWKS_URI

environmentVariables.description: Expected JWT aud claim for MCP_AUTH_MODE=resource-server. A token carrying a different audience, or no aud claim at all, is rejected. Unset skips audience validation entirely.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_OAUTH_AUDIENCE

environmentVariables.description: Set to Y (or Yes/YES, any casing) to accept the BlueCat End User License Agreement. The container refuses to start without it.
environmentVariables.name: ACCEPT_EULA

server.name: com.jithox/jithox
server.description: EU business checks: VAT/VIES, IBAN, Peppol, KBO lookup. 16 of 19 tools need no token.
server.title: Jithox EU business checks

access.chargingRule: Only accepted calls are charged. Refusals, invalid input, authentication failures, rate limits, provider outages and 'unavailable' answers cost nothing.
access.freeTier: 16 of 19 tools work anonymously, no account, no token, e.g. verify_iban, check_peppol_ready, check_vat_list, kbo_company_search, review_invoice, fetch_web_markdown.
access.paid: 3 tools (transcribe_and_slice_audio, parse_receipt_vision, monitor_sources) need a Bearer token, are prepaid EUR 0.10 per accepted call, and a human must approve the connection first.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.authentication: None required for the free tools listed above. Paid tools use a separate connection with human-approved OAuth.
boundaries: This server never sends, files or pays anything. It returns evidence and structured checks only.
A negative answer means one source returned no match at that moment, never that a company is unregistered or non-compliant.
Provider outages produce 'unavailable', never a guessed verdict.
No independent penetration test has been performed.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.commercialStatus: LIVE — the free tier is technical beta, self-service, no card. Paid tools require a human-approved connection.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.publicationStatus: Public, free tier self-service without a login.

server.name: com.jithox/jithox
server.description: Call preflight_payment before an agent pays an invoice: approval, IBAN, bank change; signed, free.
server.title: Jithox payment preflight: check an invoice payment before your AI agent pays

access.freeTier: These 9 tools answer without an account or token: preflight_payment, core_condition, verify_iban, check_peppol_ready, lookup_peppol_participant, check_payment_change, file_to_data_inspect, file_to_data_transform, check_vat_list_format.
access.paid: The other 11 tools refuse without a bearer token (HTTP 401, code payment_required) and name their price in credits. tools/list says for check_vat_list: "1 credit (EUR 0.01) per answered row; needs a bearer token."

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.authentication: None for the free tools above. The other tools answer HTTP 401 with a WWW-Authenticate Bearer challenge (scope engine:call, resource metadata https://jithox.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/mcp). The refusal points to https://jithox.com/mcp/account#connection, where a person creates the connection.
boundaries: tools/list annotates all 20 tools readOnlyHint: true and destructiveHint: false.
tools/list says for preflight_payment: "Never pays; a check that did not run is never a pass."
https://jithox.com/trust: internal testing is not an independent penetration test.

paymentPreflight.access: Free: no account and no token. tools/list says "Free, no token."; every anonymous answer measured on 2026-09-25 carried billing.charged false.
paymentPreflight.checkedToday: Rail invoice_bank: approved versus to-pay (amount, currency, payee name, account), IBAN structure and check digits, a changed bank account against ibanOnFile, the supplier country, and the Peppol participant when a peppolId is given.
paymentPreflight.notCoveredToday: Rails x402, card_or_giftcard and crypto_bridge: no rail checks run; the best answer there is review_required with reason rail_not_covered.
paymentPreflight.returns: stop, review_required or no_blockers_found, with every check, what it does not prove, and a signed evidence token (compact JWS).
paymentPreflight.verifyEvidence: POST https://jithox.com/api/v1/evidence/verify with the jws (optionally with the input and inputSalt); public keys at https://jithox.com/.well-known/jwks.json.
paymentPreflight.when: Once, before an agent moves money for a person.

server.name: com.mailbox-mcp/mailbox-mcp
server.description: Read, send, file and search email in any Gmail, Microsoft 365 or IMAP mailbox, plus its calendar.
server.title: Mailbox MCP

com.mailbox-mcp.authentication: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE. Mailbox credentials are envelope-encrypted and are never held by the client.
com.mailbox-mcp.summary: Mailbox MCP connects an assistant to a real mailbox over IMAP and SMTP, so it can read, write, file and search mail as the owner would. The mailbox has to look untouched afterwards in Outlook or webmail, and that rule decides the implementation: reading never marks a message as read, a send files exactly one copy in Sent, a delete moves to Trash, a draft is saved where another client can edit it, a move keeps flags and the internal date, and folders resolve by their special-use flag instead of by name. It archives and reports spam by role rather than by folder name, so on Gmail, with no archive folder, archiving drops the inbox label. It reads attachments: a PDF, a Word file or a spreadsheet as text, a photo as a picture. After a send, check_bounces says whether an address failed permanently or is still being retried, and check_receipts whether it was opened, even when the honest answer is that nothing came back. A diary connected as a separate step adds calendar tools: reading and searching events, free/busy, booking and moving your own time, inviting, cancelling, answering or proposing another time, and the out-of-office reply. A CardDAV address book connected to an IMAP mailbox, also separately, lets find_contact read the book beside the mailbox's own history, labelling each result's source, and adds read_contact to open one card. No contact is ever stored on the server. A mailbox with no diary or book is handed none of those tools rather than tools that refuse, so the tool count varies by mailbox.
com.mailbox-mcp.toolsNote: This list is the mail surface, which every connected mailbox gets. The calendar and contact tools are absent: each is registered only on a mailbox whose owner has connected a diary or an address book, and Outlook contacts on a Microsoft mailbox that reconnects, so listing them here would be a promise the server had not kept. find_contact is listed because every mailbox has it; a connected book improves it, and a writable one makes the contact tools five. The summary says what each adds.
worksWith: Any IMAP and SMTP mail host
Microsoft 365 and Exchange Online, over OAuth
Gmail and Google Workspace, with an app password
Microsoft 365 and Google calendars, over OAuth

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.account_required: A free Pantry Butler account. No approval process, no waitlist.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.auth: OAuth 2.1. Clients register themselves (RFC 7591 dynamic client registration) and authorize with PKCE S256 — no token to paste and no key to issue by hand. Discovery is the standard one: an unauthenticated call to /mcp returns 401 with a WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata pointer to https://thepantrybutler.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. Scopes are read and write; write implies read. Long-lived bearer tokens from https://thepantrybutler.com/connect still work for scripts and self-hosted clients.

headers.description: DocsMint Cloud remote at https://docsmint.com/mcp; no self-hosted server is required. Discovery advertises /oauth/authorize, /oauth/token, and active DCR at https://docsmint.com/oauth/register. Metadata supports the code response type, authorization_code grant only, no token-endpoint client authentication, and PKCE S256; CIMD is not part of the contract. Access tokens last one hour, have no refresh token, and are bound by browser consent to a workspace, optional category, and requested scopes. API-key clients can use Authorization: Bearer <key> with a workspace-bound or category-scoped credential created at https://docsmint.com/mcp/connect?source=mcp_registry. Credential management requires a browser session. For self-hosting, use the stdio package with your own API and API key; it does not install the Cloud OAuth server.

server.name: io.github.Nizoka/pdfnative-mcp
server.description: PDF MCP server: generate PDF/A, sign & verify PAdES (LTV), forms, merge, split, encrypt. 28 tools
server.title: pdfnative MCP — PDF generation, PAdES signing & introspection

environmentVariables.description: Absolute path of a sandboxed directory where outputMode='file' may write PDFs. Unset: every tool returns base64 only (file output disabled).
environmentVariables.name: PDFNATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Opt-in content-addressed response cache directory (SHA-256 keyed, 1h TTL, 256 MiB LRU, plaintext at rest). Never caches encrypt/decrypt, sign, timestamp, add_ltv, update_metadata, encrypted builds or file output.
environmentVariables.name: PDFNATIVE_MCP_CACHE_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Serve Streamable HTTP on this loopback port instead of stdio (MCP 2026-07-28, stateless). Unauthenticated unless PDFNATIVE_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN is set.
environmentVariables.name: PDFNATIVE_MCP_PORT

environmentVariables.description: Opt-in bearer token for the HTTP transport (>= 16 chars, no whitespace). When set, /mcp requires 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' or answers 401. Never logged.
environmentVariables.name: PDFNATIVE_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: Per-stream FlateDecode decompression cap in bytes (zip-bomb mitigation; default 104857600 = 100 MiB). Integer >= 1024; an invalid value refuses to start the server.
environmentVariables.name: PDFNATIVE_MCP_MAX_INFLATE_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: http(s) URL of the RFC 3161 timestamp authority used by sign_pdf timestamp=true and timestamp_pdf (PAdES B-T / B-LTA). Unset: those calls fail with TSA_NOT_CONFIGURED and no network request is made. Tool arguments can never supply a URL.
environmentVariables.name: PDFNATIVE_MCP_TSA_URL

environmentVariables.description: Optional Authorization header value sent to the TSA (e.g. 'Basic ...' or 'Bearer ...'). Never logged or echoed.
environmentVariables.name: PDFNATIVE_MCP_TSA_AUTH

environmentVariables.description: 'ocsp', 'crl' or 'ocsp,crl': enables online revocation collection for add_ltv mode='online' (PAdES B-LT). Unset: that mode fails with REVOCATION_NOT_CONFIGURED; mode='offline' stays fully offline. Requires PDFNATIVE_MCP_NETWORK_ALLOWED_HOSTS.
environmentVariables.name: PDFNATIVE_MCP_REVOCATION

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated allow-list of OCSP / CRL responder hosts ('host', 'host:port' or '*.suffix'). Mandatory when PDFNATIVE_MCP_REVOCATION is set: responder URLs found in certificates are fetched only if the host matches (http(s) only, no credentials, no redirects, internal addresses rejected unless listed verbatim).
environmentVariables.name: PDFNATIVE_MCP_NETWORK_ALLOWED_HOSTS

environmentVariables.description: Per-request timeout for TSA / OCSP / CRL calls in milliseconds, 1000-120000 (default 10000).
environmentVariables.name: PDFNATIVE_MCP_NETWORK_TIMEOUT_MS

server.description: MCP server enabling AI clients to interact with any MediaWiki wiki through standard tools
server.title: MediaWiki MCP Server

environmentVariables.description: Path to your configuration file
environmentVariables.name: CONFIG

environmentVariables.description: Set to 'true' to allow HTTP startup when config.json has static credentials. Otherwise the server refuses to start, preventing silent shared-identity fallback for unauthenticated requests.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_ALLOW_STATIC_FALLBACK

environmentVariables.description: Byte cap for the content bodies and result blocks tools return (wikitext, rendered HTML, diffs, statement and row listings). An oversized response is truncated with a trailing marker describing what was left out.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_CONTENT_MAX_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: Hard cap on the base64-encoded size of a get-file-data response. A transport/safety backstop; callers tune actual size with the tool's width parameter. Over-cap responses error rather than truncate.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_FILE_DATA_MAX_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: Minimum severity for logger output (stderr telemetry and sendLoggingMessage broadcast). Invalid values fail loudly on first log call.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_LOG_LEVEL

environmentVariables.description: Maximum HTTP request body size on the StreamableHTTP transport. Accepts size strings like 1mb or 512kb.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_MAX_REQUEST_BODY

environmentVariables.description: Set to 'true' to expose Prometheus metrics at GET /metrics on the HTTP transport. Has no effect on the stdio transport.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_METRICS

environmentVariables.description: Additional allowed redirect URIs for hosted-proxy client registration: comma-separated exact URIs (which must include a host) and https prefix patterns ending in /*. Loopback, claude.ai, and verified first-party clients (ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code) are always allowed; unset means no additional clients.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_OAUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECTS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated additional client_id document hosts trusted for CIMD (bare host or host:port). Verified first-party hosts are always trusted.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_OAUTH_CIMD_ALLOWED_HOSTS

environmentVariables.description: Override the default OAuth credentials store path. Default: ~/.config/mediawiki-mcp/credentials.json on Linux/macOS, %APPDATA%\mediawiki-mcp\credentials.json on Windows.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS_FILE

environmentVariables.description: Set to '1' to skip launching a browser during the OAuth dance and log the auth URL to stderr instead. Useful in headless environments and CI.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_OAUTH_NO_BROWSER

environmentVariables.description: Path to the hosted OAuth proxy's encrypted state file, which lets sign-ins survive restarts. Default: proxy-store.enc under the mediawiki-mcp config dir; /app/data/proxy-store.enc in the Docker image.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_OAUTH_PROXY_STORE_FILE

environmentVariables.description: Override the request-derived public URL used in the protected-resource discovery doc and WWW-Authenticate header. Set this when running behind a proxy that rewrites the request Host.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_PUBLIC_URL

environmentVariables.description: Maximum milliseconds to wait for in-flight /mcp calls to drain on SIGTERM/SIGINT before exiting. Capped at 600000.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS

environmentVariables.description: Type of MCP server transport
environmentVariables.name: MCP_TRANSPORT

environmentVariables.description: Memory cap on the server-side fetch used by upload-file-from-url and update-file-from-url. Files larger than this are routed to the wiki's own copy-upload instead of being buffered by the server. Guards this server's memory, not the wiki's $wgMaxUploadSize.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: Port used for StreamableHTTP transport
environmentVariables.name: PORT

environmentVariables.name: EUROSTAT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS

environmentVariables.description: How long a fetched catalogue TOC stays usable before the next catalogue call refreshes it, in milliseconds. Defaults to 12 hours.
environmentVariables.name: EUROSTAT_TOC_CACHE_TTL_MS

environmentVariables.description: HTTP timeout for one eurostat_download_dataset transfer, in milliseconds. Held separate from EUROSTAT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS because a bulk body streams for minutes where a metadata call answers in seconds. Defaults to 2 minutes.
environmentVariables.name: EUROSTAT_BULK_TIMEOUT_MS

environmentVariables.description: Byte budget for one eurostat_download_dataset transfer, counted on the decoded TSV rather than on the wire. environmentVariables.description: Anthropic API key. environmentVariables.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

environmentVariables.name: DATABASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: Path to a `config.yaml` holding the rest of the engine's settings — additional stores, model selection per purpose, and the `mcp.write.enabled_stores` allowlist that turns the write tools on.
environmentVariables.name: PARTICLES_CONFIG

toolSurface.writeGate: mcp.write.enabled_stores is empty by default; a store must be named there before any write tool is registered.
